On Monday, Reuters carried a story by Maggie Fox, their Health and Science Correspondent, that CNN ran under the headline: Stronger pot causes policy shift.

Reporters have no control over headlines, but CNN's header accurately reflected the essence of most news stories, new facts cause a change in policy.

The article also included the standard elements. Government officials are quoted, citing supporting data. To show balance, the article includes very brief quotes from a group that opposes government policies.

Unfortunately, what the article did not include was the basic fact-checking that would have shown that there are no new facts and there is no new policy. I have repeatedly said that the best two-word explanation for cannabis prohibition is bad journalism, and this article is a classic example of thinly disguised prohibitionist propaganda.
and for another example from Reuters see
Almost every sentence can be usefully deconstructed. It has it all. After the drug war ends, this article should be studied in every journalism school so that we can understand how millions of Americans were arrested and journalism, science and medicine were highjacked by the police state.
Thanks, Maggie.
See
Embarrassing Questions: If It Was Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Saddam, Why Isn't It Wrong to Lie to Justify the War on Cannabis Users? Analysis by Richard Cowan

Stronger pot may lead to reefer madness
(MarijuanaNews note: This headline was on the Yahoo/Reuters site)

July 19, 2004
From Reuters

By Maggie Fox, Health and Science Correspondent

(MarijuanaNews note: Fox is no cub reporter. This is her beat, but Reuters has a very mixed track record. Fox actually made a slightly positive contribution to really bad series of reports by Reuters.
See
Marijuana Is Addictive; The Internet Is Addictive; Therefore This Site Is A Hard Drug -- New Study

In this next story she failed to note that the reported changes fell within the margin of error for the survey. In short, she took the prohibitionists word for it.)
See
The Spin Is Beginning To Wobble On The " Latest Teen Drug Use " Survey. Czar Is " Greatly Encouraged " By Poll Showing Heroin Use By 12th Graders At All Time High.

WASHINGTON (Reuters) - Alarmed by reports that marijuana is becoming more potent than ever and that children are trying it at younger and younger ages, U.S. officials are changing their drug policies.
(MarijuanaNews note: Beginning with the claim that officials are alarmed sets the tone and indicates an acceptance of the official position.)

Pot is no longer the gentle weed of the 1960s and may pose a greater threat than cocaine or even heroin because so many more people use it.

(MarijuanaNews note: This is such a common cliché in prohibitionist propaganda that I even parodied it in a headline in August of 1998, almost exactly six years ago. At that time I dealt with most of the substantive points in the Reuters article. I also cite Zimmer and Morgan's 1997 book, Marijuana Myths, Marijuana Facts.
See
Marijuana Prohibition And Potency, Price, And Safety -- " Is Marijuana Stronger Now Than It Was Back In the '60s,
When Everyone Thought It Was Harmless? "

On page 134, at the beginning of their Chapter 19, The Potency of Marijuana they quote former Drug Czar William Bennett, whose protégé John Walters is the current Czar. Ten years ago, in 1994, Bennett claimed, If people confessing to marijuana use in the late 60s  sucked in on one of today's marijuana cigarettes they'd fall down backwards.

In addition, Zimmer and Morgan cite other examples of this claim dating back to 1974. In short, there is nothing new about the claims that marijuana is becoming more potent than ever.

Brian Bennett a good guy and no kin to the former Czar found a quote from 1980:
 " Marijuana is up to ten times more potent than that smoked a decade ago. " Marijuana: The Myth of Harmlessness Goes Up in Smoke, Saturday Evening Post, Jul/Aug 1980, p.34

On the other hand, there is a recent study that contradict the entire premise of the article, and yet this report was completely ignored by Fox. [In fairness to Reuters, the AP made a mess of that story.]
See
European Study Shows Potency of Prohibitionist Propaganda. CBS and The AP Lie to the American People About the Dutch. Surprise!

The second part, saying that marijuana may pose a greater threat than cocaine or even heroin because so many more people use it is quite illogical and entirely vicious.

Let's be very clear about this. The Reuters Health and Science correspondent is telling the children of America that the risks in using heroin and cocaine are the same as the risks in using marijuana.

The stated basis of thisclaim is that so many more people use marijuana. If the prevalence of use was the measure of danger, then caffeine would be the biggest drug problem in the world.)

So officials at the National Institutes of Health and at the White House are hoping to shift some of the focus in research and enforcement from " hard " drugs such as cocaine and heroin to marijuana.

(MarijuanaNews note: First, note the quotation marks around hard. Again creating the impression that the risks in marijuana are comparable to those in heroin and cocaine.

Second, the claim that propagandists are hoping to shift some of the focus in research and enforcement to marijuana ignores the fact that the current emphasis in both research and enforcement is already on marijuana.

In 2002, the last year for which we have the arrest data, the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Uniform Crime Reports (UCR), out of 1,538,800 drug arrests, marijuana arrests totaled almost 700,000, of which 88% were for simple possession.

See
NORML Reports Marijuana Arrests For 2002 Near Record High Pot Smokers Arrested In America At A Rate Of One Every 45 Seconds Plus Analysis by Richard Cowan.

Bureau of Justice Statisticsdata show that there were less than half a million arrests for heroin and cocaine. How many more marijuana users would Fox have arrested?

Nor is this emphasis on marijuana new.
From July of 1999 see
Drug War Priorities Shift From Hard Drugs To Marijuana, Arrest Figures Reveal

As for NIDA research most of that is already focused on finding any risk however remote in cannabis use, not hard drugs.
See
Institute of Medicine Report on Medical Marijuana Contradicts Assumptions for NIDA Monkeyshines. Special to MarijuanaNews
and
As Predicted, NIDA Buys Its Press Release: " Marijuana has as much potential for abuse  as cocaine and heroin. "
and
Media Alert: Watch for New NIDA Study Claiming Animal Tests Prove Marijuana Is Addictive. Great Marketing of Prohibitionist Propaganda.
and

and
New Media Merger: Washington Post Merges With NIDA.)

Moreover, NIDA blocks research on the medical use of cannabis as we will see on links below.)

While drug use overall is falling among children and teens, the officials worry that the children who are trying pot are doing so at ever-younger ages, when their brains and bodies are vulnerable to dangerous side effects.

" Most people have been led to believe that marijuana is a soft drug, not a drug that causes serious problems, " John Walters, head of the White House Office of National Drug Control Policy, said in an interview.
(MarijuanaNews note: Again, even this line is not entirely new. In 1998, then HHS Secretary said, The perception of this country is that marijuana is safe, that it's a soft drug.)
From August 1998, see
Shalala Says That Parents Are Wrong To Be RelievedThat Their Children Are Using Marijuana Instead Of Heroin!
Survey Results From California Do Not Support Party Line, So They Are Buried.

" (But) marijuana today is a much more serious problem than the vast majority of Americans understand. If you told people that one in five of 12- to 17-year-olds who ever used marijuana in their lives need treatment, I don't think people would remotely understand it. "

(MarijuanaNews note: There is a major story behind this claim that a real Health and Science Correspondent would want to report, but not this one, apparently.)
See
Walters Tells a New Lie. Oh Happy Day! People Need Treatment If They Are Sent to Treatment, By Definition. And How Do They Treat Marijuana Addicts? We Couldn't Make This Up, But They Did.

JUMP IN POT-RELATED DETOX

The number of children and teen-agers in treatment for marijuana dependence and abuse has jumped 142 percent since 1992, the National Centre on Addiction and Substance Abuse at Columbia University reported in April.

(MarijuanaNews note: Citing CASA seems to add another layer of authority for these claims, but CASA is just citing the government's oft-repeated claims.)
See
Columbia University Prostitutes Itself. JAMA Publishes Racist Claptrap. The Lancet Upholds Its Standards.

According to the report, children and teens are three times more likely to be in treatment for marijuana abuse than for alcohol, and six times likelier to be in treatment for marijuana than for all other illegal drugs combined.
(MarijuanaNews note: Of course, they are in treatment because they are sent by the courts and schools, not necessarily because they need treatment. And does this treatment really work?)
See
Conference On Rehab Racketeers Tied To Bush Will Raise Important Issues: Saving Children From Drug Treatment Abuse. Saving DEAland from Drug War Lite. A Conference That Should Embarrass Washington.
and
The Real Data On Teen Marijuana " Abuse Treatment " What The Media Don't Tell Us: " Half of marijuana treatment admissions were referred through the criminal justice system. " -- Analysis By Richard Cowan

And it found the age of youths using marijuana is falling. The teens aged 12 to 17 said on average they started trying marijuana at 13-1/2. The same survey found that adults aged 18 to 25 had first tried it at 16.
(MarijuanaNews note: Mightn't this suggest that cannabis prohibition and all of the propaganda supporting it is actually counterproductive?)
See
John Walters Says, Prescription Drug Abuse Is The Second Largest Illicit Drug Problem After Cannabis, Of Course! Different Measures for Success and Failure. Seeking New Victims.

For National Institute on Drug Abuse director Dr. Nora Volkow the final straw was a report her institute published in May in the Journal of the American Medical Association showing the steady growth in the potency of cannabis seized in raids.
(MarijuanaNews note: The JAMA published NIDA's version of the data, and NIDA is convinced. However, I am genuinely puzzled by their handling of the data. The NIDA/JAMA articlesays,

A number of factors could have led to increases in addiction potential, operating either independently or conjointly. The first is increased marijuana potency. The potency of delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol ( delta 9-THC ) in confiscated marijuana from police seizures increased by 66% from 3.08% in 1992 to 5.11% in 2002.34,35 Average potency of delta 9-THC in these studies was consistently calculated as the simple arithmetic mean ( ie, the sum of the delta 9-THC concentrations divided by the number of seizures ), which is more useful in discerning changes over time relative to normalized averages. (emphasis added)

As this indicates, Mississippi's Potency Project publishes two numbers. The first is the average THC content of all of the seizures, regardless of quantity. The second is the average of all the seizures based on weight. The first number would give equal importance to an ounce and a ton. That reminds me of the old joke about the butcher who sold meat that he claimed was half rabbit and half horse. That is, it contained one rabbit and one horse.

Sometimes there is a significant difference in the two numbers; sometimes there is not. 1984 the weight adjusted average THC content was almost 4%. Ten years later that number was just 0.61%. This variation indicates that there are serious problems in the sampling process.

However, the second number does give some indication of what really reaches the market, and it seems unlikely that, as the NIDA/JAMA article assumes, young people are buying the most expensive cannabis.)

According to the University of Mississippi's Marijuana Potency Project, average levels of THC, the active ingredient in marijuana, rose steadily from 3.5 percent in 1988 to more than 7 percent in 2003.
See
Dan Forbes Documents Walters Lies About Potency. Understanding That The War On Cannabis Is Built On Lies Is Key to Understanding More Than Just Drug War.
and also Brian Bennett again:
http://www.briancbennett.com/charts/fed-data/stronger-weed.htm

Volkow said many studies have shown the brain has its own so-called endogenous cannabinoids. These molecules are similar in structure to the active ingredients in marijuana and are involved in a range of activities and emotions ranging from eye function to pain regulation and anxiety.

Getting into the Brain
(MarijuanaNews note: Everything here is speculative. Notice the qualifiers.)

Brain cells have receptors -- molecular doorways designed specifically to interact with these cannabinoids.

The cannabinoids in marijuana may use these ready-made doorways into brain cells and this is why they cause a high and reduce pain sensations. But Volkow believes the effects may go beyond the general feeling of well-being that most marijuana users seek.

" I would predict that stronger pot makes the brain less likely to respond to endogenous cannabinoids, " Volkow said in an interview. The effects could be especially marked in young brains still growing and learning how to respond to stimuli, she said.

While the research so far is inconclusive, Volkow believes that cannabinoids affect the developing brain and that stronger pot, combined with earlier use, could make children and teens anxious, unmotivated or perhaps even psychotic.
See
Parents The Pro-Drug? Are Nagging Parents Driving Their Kids to Drink? Driving Schizophrenics Paranoid? Can We Drive the Media to Think?

As an analogy, Volkow said opiate addicts are more sensitive to pain, as their overuse of drugs have raised the threshold at which the body responds and their own bodies produce fewer natural opiates.

NIDA is seeking proposals from researchers who want to investigate such possibilities for cannabis, she said.
See
More Proof That The Drug War Is Really A War On Cannabis. Plus: Sabotaging Medical Cannabis Research And Lying About It. Analysis by Richard Cowan
and
Scientist say marijuana research is blocked

Proponents of legalising marijuana disagree with the official line.

Krissy Oechslin of the Marijuana Policy Project disputes the finding that cannabis products are stronger.
(MarijuanaNews note: One should not blame Ms Oechslin for any inadequacy in the response, because there is no way to know what she told Fox.)
" They make it sound like the THC levels in marijuana were almost nonexistent, but no one would have smoked it then if that was true, " she said.

" And there's evidence that the stronger the THC, the less of it a person smokes. I don't want to say it's good for you, but I'll say (more potent marijuana) is less bad for you. "

While Walters stresses that drug abusers are patients and not criminals, he hopes to crack down more on producers. And he says, there is a way to go in getting cooperation from local law enforcement officials. " For many in enforcement, marijuana is still 'kiddie dope', " Walters said.
(MarijuanaNews note: Excuse me! Drug abusers are patients and not criminals ??? What about the millions of Americans who have arrest records and even the medical patients who have been sent to prison for using cannabis? They are by definition criminals.)

Walters is quick to stress he does not want to overreact.

We shouldn't be victims of reefer madness, he said, referring to the 1930s propaganda film " Reefer Madness " that became a 1970s cult classic for its over-the-top scenes of marijuana turning teens into homicidal maniacs.
(MarijuanaNews note: No, he was not referring to the movie, but this article. Or maybe he was referring to NIDA's Volkow who was just quoted as saying that cannabinoids could make children and teens anxious, unmotivated or perhaps even psychotic.

This is the final outrage in this garbage, trying to make Walters look moderate. Reuters should be ashamed. CNN should sue them for fraud..)
